To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We analyze and optimize the throughput of multicore processors with power- and thermal constraints by exploiting per-core power gating, dynamic voltage scaling, and core-to-core frequency variation.

(i) power gating of idle cores can significantly improve the throughput of a power- and thermalconstrained multicore processor running applications with limited degree of parallelism, (ii) supply voltage and frequency scaling of active cores can improve the throughput of the power- and thermal constrained multicore processors, and (iii) considering within-die process variation can improve the throughput further.

(1) optimizing the number of cores and operating frequency of a multicore processor improves the throughput of the processor by up to 16%, and (2) exploiting core-to-core delay variations in a multicored processor improves the throughput by up to 75%.
